units.text: INT. SWIFTLINE DELIVERY WAREHOUSE - MORNING
We see a huge warehouse with many shelves and conveyor belts.
Its early morning and the lights are still turning on one by one.
BARRY, 40s, a shift supervisor who thinks he is very important, walks in carrying a coffee and a clipboard.
CLOSE ON Barry's name tag, which says "BARRY - SUPERVISOR" in big letters.
Good morning team! Big day today!
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Nobody answers.
We see NADINE, 30s, tired, sitting on a pallet jack eating a granola bar, and ROBIN, 20s, who uses they/them pronouns, scrolling on their phone near the sorting belt.
Its 6 AM Barry.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: And whats that mean? It means the early bird gets the worm!
units.name: BARRY

units.text: I dont even like worms.
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: What was that Robin?
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Nothing. Good morning.
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: Barry nods happily and puts his coffee down on a stack of boxes marked FRAGILE, then walks to the control panel and presses a green button and the belt starts to move slowly, and Nadine stands up and stretches while Robin puts their phone in their pocket and walks to the end of the belt and picks up the first package, and Barry checks his clipboard and looks very pleased with himself while a forklift beeps somewhere far away.
Okay everybody listen up. Today is a normal day. Nothing special. Just normal packages, normal routes, normal everything.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: You said normal three times.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: Because its normal!
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Nadine looks at Robin.
Robin looks at Nadine.
They both look at Barry.
He's lying about something.
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: Obviously.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: We see the belt carry a small brown box down the line.
It is the only box that is not scanned by the machine.
CLOSE ON the box.
It has a red sticker that says "DO NOT OPEN - PRIVATE".
Barry what is this?
units.name: NADINE

units.text: Its nothing. Just a regular box. Put it back.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: It doesnt have a barcode.
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: Some boxes dont have barcodes Robin that is a known thing.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Robin lifts the box off the belt.
It is light.
Something inside RATTLES softly.
Barry's face goes white and he drops his clipboard, which CLATTERS on the concrete floor.
Oh no. He's sweating.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: Please put it down. Please. Both of you.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Is it a bomb?
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: Its not a bomb!
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Then open it.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: I cant let you open it!
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Nadine takes the box from Robin and in one move she tears the red sticker and rips the tape.
Robin leans in, Barry covers his eyes with both hands, and a forklift driver in the distance honks twice for no reason.
CLOSE ON the open box.
Inside are forty-two tiny bottles of hotel shampoo, six stolen name tags from other supervisors, and a laminated sign that says "WORLDS BEST BOSS".
Silence.
These are the name tags from Dayton.
units.name: NADINE

units.text: Barry. Did you make yourself an award?
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: It was going to be a surprise.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: For who?
units.name: NADINE

units.text: For me. At the Friday meeting. I was going to have you all give it to me.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: I want to be mad but I'm mostly impressed.
units.name: ROBIN

units.text: Hey everybody! Barry made himself an award!
units.name: NADINE
paren: to the group of the whole warehouse, shouting

units.text: From far away in the building we hear a slow, growing round of applause, and a lone forklift honks.
Barry sits down on the pallet jack and puts his face in his hands.
Can I at least keep the shampoo.
units.name: BARRY

units.text: Nadine tosses him one small bottle.
Robin sets the laminated sign on top of Barry's head like a crown.
Congratulations boss.
units.name: ROBIN
